questions.q: Who occupied the highest position in the Mughal social structure?
questions.a: The Emperor and the nobles. A student answering "merchants" shows they are confusing the political elite with the business class.

questions.q: Why is it accurate to call the Mughal social structure "hierarchical"?
questions.a: It means society was organized in levels, from the most powerful at the top to the laborers at the bottom. An answer focusing only on "jobs" misses the point that these levels dictated power and influence.

questions.q: If a drought destroyed the crops in a village, how would this affect an artisan living in a city?
questions.a: The artisan would suffer because the peasants would have no surplus to sell or trade, meaning the artisan would lose their customers and raw materials. An answer saying "it wouldn't affect them" shows a lack of understanding of economic interdependence.

questions.q: How did the Bhakti and Sufi movements challenge the traditional social order of the time?
questions.a: They preached equality and devotion, which questioned the strict boundaries of the caste system and social classes. A wrong answer suggests they were purely political movements, ignoring their social/spiritual impact.

questions.q: Is it fair to say the Mughal economy was only based on farming? Justify your answer.
questions.a: No, because while farming was the base, the economy relied heavily on a large class of artisans, weavers, and merchants who processed goods and traded them. Ignoring the "middle" class of the hierarchy leads to an incomplete view.

questions.q: If you were a merchant in a Mughal city, what evidence would you need to show that your business was part of a larger, complex society?
questions.a: Evidence would include the variety of goods sold (crafts vs. food), the reliance on different transport routes, and the use of money or credit. A poor answer would just list items without explaining the "system" of trade.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Mughal society and economy refers to the organized way people lived, worked, and interacted during the period of the Mughal Empire in India, ______ by a distinct hierarchy of social classes and diverse professional groups.
Fill in the blank: ______ about your own school: there are teachers, administrators, and students, all working together to keep the school running.
What is Mughal society and economy? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Mughal society and economy refers to the organized way people lived, worked, and interacted during the period of the Mughal Empire in India, characterized by a distinct hierarchy of social classes and diverse professional groups.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Mughal society and economy?
questions.a: Students often think the Mughal Empire was purely a military state and ignore the "everyday" economy.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to categorize different groups of people into the Mughal social hierarchy and describe how the economy relied on the cooperation between urban artisans, merchants, and rural farmers.
